R81 may not merge under existing policy. Compatibility failed on C7. W9 authorizes C7 only for R80 and expires immediately when the candidate changes, so it cannot cover R81. Tomorrow’s calendar expiry, unchanged consumers, and passing compensation do not cure that mismatch. The supplied compile and affected test successes remain valid but do not satisfy compatibility. Archiving the report preserves evidence; saying ‘compatibility passed’ would misrepresent it. R81 needs either a compatibility fix with fresh passing evidence or an authorized exception explicitly covering that candidate; this assessment grants neither.

The smallest correction is to change the trusted required aggregate’s decision predicate: consume the raw checker outcome and candidate-bound evidence plus the exception record, instead of relying only on job results. Ensure it runs after upstream failures and remains blocking. Preserve report collection. Distinguish three dispositions: actual compatibility success; compatibility failed/excepted with merge permitted by a policy-valid exception; and blocked for unexcepted failure or missing/invalid evidence. Validate exception authority, exact candidate and finding, compensation, and both time-based and change-triggered expiry. A green aggregate for a valid exception must mean ‘merge permitted by exception,’ never ‘compatibility passed.’

Proposed validation should exercise the real continue-on-error path: C7 with W9 at R81 must block despite successful conclusions and job results. Also reject an absent, expired, unauthorized, wrong-finding, or compensation-unsatisfied exception, changed consumers, and missing checker evidence even with an otherwise matching exception. Include positive controls for genuine checker success and a synthetic policy-valid exact-candidate exception: the latter permits merge while retaining failed/excepted evidence. Assert raw outcome, reported disposition, and final required status. These are proposed checks, not executed results; preserve the established exception policy.
